og.title: Center for Energy-Smart Electronic Systems (ES2)
og.description: The Center for Energy-Smart Electronic Systems (ES2) provides a cross-disciplinary approach to optimizing energy use and cooling in electronic systems and data centers. ES2's mission is to develop systematic methodologies for operating dynamic, predictable, self-sensing, and self-regulating electronic systems that can be verified in real time.Thousands of data centers across the United States provide the infrastructure to handle a wide spectrum of information and processing needs for the government, military, business, and industry. Their services are critical for entertainment, e-business, e-governance, finances, cloud computing, social media, health care, and fitness. Massive amounts of energy are required to power and cool these facilities. Worldwide, about half of the energy they consume is wasted due to inefficiencies in the system and operational practices.ES2's researchers bring together expertise in computer science and mechanical and electrical engineering to provide a holistic approach to making electronic systems and data centers more energy efficient. ES2 student researchers work with faculty and industry partners to prepare for careers in this dynamically evolving sector, and help companies develop solutions that benefit their businesses and society.ES2 envisions the creation and operation of energy-optimized data centers and electronic systems with:Smart allocation and distribution of IT load and dynamic IT capacity provisioning.Smart integration of controlled, on-demand cooling.Smart elimination of energy waste and inefficiencies.Smart use of stored energy in data centers.

checks.label: HTTPS (required for service workers)
checks.why: HTTPS is required for service workers and most install prompts.

checks.label: Web app manifest declared
checks.why: A web app manifest is required for installability and controls how the app appears when launched.

checks.label: Service worker registered
checks.why: A service worker is what makes offline access, caching, and background sync possible.

checks.label: Theme color declared
checks.why: Theme color controls the browser chrome/status-bar color when the site is installed or bookmarked.

checks.label: Apple touch icon (iOS/bookmark icon)
checks.why: iOS uses this icon for home-screen bookmarks and "Add to Home Screen" — without it the icon falls back to a screenshot.

checks.label: Manifest fetched and parsed successfully
checks.why: A manifest that fails to parse cannot drive installability or launch behavior even if the link is present.

checks.label: Manifest declares a maskable icon
checks.why: A maskable icon lets the OS safely crop/mask the app icon on different device shapes without clipping content.

checks.label: Service worker is active (not just registered)
checks.why: An active service worker (not just registered) is what actually intercepts requests and serves cached content.

checks.label: Service worker controls this page load
checks.why: A controlling service worker means THIS page load is being served/intercepted, not just a future one.

checks.label: Meets basic installability criteria
checks.evidence: no readable web app manifest; no service worker registered
checks.why: Determines whether the browser can realistically offer "Add to Home Screen" / install, based on manifest + service worker + HTTPS together.
